headline_item.author: Amy Nordrum

Every year, the editors at MIT Technology Review select 35 of the world’s top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors to honor as our newest class of Innovators Under 35. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations.

We’re on the hunt for researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to some of the most formidable problems society faces, including human disease and climate change. We also recognize those who have made clever and useful inventions,

headlines.title_zh: 堪萨斯城叫停摩天数据中心项目
headlines.title_en: Developers Wanted to Build a High-Rise Data Center. Kansas City Blocked It.
headlines.author: Tiffany Hsu
headlines.event_summary_zh: 堪萨斯城市议会因社区抗议与规划争议，全票否决了一项拟建的20层高层数据中心开发计划
headlines.event_summary_en: The Kansas City Council unanimously rejected a proposal to build a 20-story data center in a historic district. The project faced significant local opposition due to concerns over urban footprint, energy consumption, and the demolition of historic landmarks, leading to the rejection after over 400 letters of protest.
core_facts_zh: 【核心事件】堪萨斯城市议会（Kansas City Council）在美国密苏里州堪萨斯城市中心：全票否决了一项拟拆除历史建筑并改建为20层高密度数据中心的开发计划
【起因与机理】当地居民对数据中心的高耗能属性及垂直化建设模式持强烈抵制态度，且对项目背后的税务激励合理性存疑
【核心事实细节】核心争议在于AI数据中心选址向城市核心区高密度扩张的社会阻力。
【各方立场与态度】城市中心算力基础设施建设面临严峻的合规与公众接纳度考验。
core_facts_en: [Core Event] Kansas City Council (Downtown Kansas City, Missouri): Unanimously blocked a proposal to develop a 20-story data center
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Local pushback against high energy demands, urban density concerns, and skepticism regarding private equity tax incentive maneuvers
[Key Metrics] Austin told one trade publication that, at $183 million, he expected construction to exceed the average cost of building a suburban facility.
[Key Position & Outlook] Infrastructure developers face mounting regulatory and social acceptance hurdles for urban compute hubs.
headlines.industry_impact_zh: 随着AI算力需求向城市核心区渗透，数据中心选址正从边缘化土地向高密度垂直空间转型，但与传统城市景观的兼容性博弈将成为该产业落地的最大非技术障碍。此案例预示着未来算力基础设施建设需在‘分布式紧凑设计’与‘本地社区环境合规性’之间建立更严苛的平衡机制。
headlines.industry_impact_en: As AI compute demands migrate toward urban cores, the tension between data center density and municipal urban planning is intensifying. This rejection signals that future infrastructure deployments will face escalating regulatory scrutiny, forcing operators to prioritize social license and architectural integration over sheer vertical capacity.

headlines.title_zh: 犹他大学突破神经接口假肢技术
headlines.title_en: Cutting-edge prosthetics allow researchers to probe the human mind
headlines.author: Jessica Hamzelou
headlines.event_summary_zh: 犹他大学研究团队完成一项创新假肢临床试验，受试者可通过植入神经电极实现假肢的精细操控与感官反馈
headlines.event_summary_en: Researchers at the University of Utah are conducting a clinical trial on advanced neural-interface prosthetics. By implanting electrodes into the nerves of the participant's arm, the technology enables both motorized control and sensory feedback, marking a significant step toward real-world independent use of bionic limbs.
core_facts_zh: 【核心事件】犹他大学（University of Utah）研究团队在神经工程临床试验环境：通过神经电极植入实现假肢的精细感知与运动反馈，并验证了居家环境下的独立操作能力
【起因与机理】旨在攻克假肢触觉缺失与控制精度难题，同时研究脑神经反馈对假肢操控的影响
【核心事实细节】基于神经电极植入的闭环操控假肢技术。
【行业影响与走向】研究重点转向神经反馈对假肢性能与大脑塑性的协同影响。
core_facts_en: [Core Event] University of Utah research team: Enabled precise prosthetic control and sensory feedback via nerve-implanted electrodes, validated for independent home use
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To solve limitations in tactile feedback and motor precision, and to study neuroplasticity in prosthetic integration
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Closed-loop prosthetic technology based on implanted neural electrodes.
[Key Position & Outlook] Focus shifting to neuroplasticity and the synergy between sensory feedback and motor control.
headlines.industry_impact_zh: 此项研究标志着假肢技术从单纯的机械代偿转向神经深度整合阶段，电极植入的生物相容性与长期信号稳定性是后续产业化转化的核心技术护城河。商业端需关注其在神经反馈闭环系统上的突破，这直接决定了未来生物医学工程领域中人机融合形态的可及性。
headlines.industry_impact_en: This research signifies a transition from passive mechanical prosthetics to deep neural integration. The technical moat lies in the biocompatibility and long-term signal stability of the implanted electrodes, which will define the commercial viability of future human-machine fusion platforms.

titans.event_context_zh:
GPU 操作。

它启动一系列操作来进行注意力、矩阵相乘、标准化、采样、数据移动和其他工作。

如果没有 CUDA Graph，CPU 会单独准备并提交这些操作。

每次启动仅增加少量开销，但逐个令牌解码会对每个生成的令牌重复类似的序列。

这造成了一个奇怪的瓶颈。

有些内核只需几微秒即可完成。 GPU 可以在 CPU 提交下一个内核之前完成一个内核。

这会在探查器跟踪中留下空白空间。这些差距不是模型计算。它们显示 GPU 正在等待下一个操作。

CUDA Graph 改变了这项工作到达 GPU 的方式。

运行时捕获一次可重复的操作序列，包括它们的依赖项。稍后的迭代通过一个图启动重放捕获的序列，而不是单独提交每个操作。

需要明确的是，内核本身并没有变得更快。

此外，模型不会变小，并且前向传递执行几乎相同的计算。

大部分收益来自于消除内核之间的 CPU 启动工作。

这在 LLM 解码期间特别有用。

每个解码步骤为每个序列处理一个新标记。这会产生许多短的、重复的 GPU 操作，其中启动开销可能成为总延迟的一个有意义的部分。

预填充通常表现不同。

较大的提示可以让 GPU 进行更多并行工作，从而生成运行时间更长的内核。当这些内核已经让 GPU 忙碌时，减少启动开销就不那么重要了。

还有一个权衡。

捕获的图在每次重放时都需要相同的内核序列、稳定的参数、固定的内存地址和兼容的执行结构。

推理服务器可处理不同的批量大小以及不同的预填充、混合和解码工作负载。一张捕获的图无法有效覆盖每条执行路径。

因此，vLLM 和 TensorRT-LLM 等引擎可以捕获几种常见执行情况和批量大小的图表。

当实时批次与捕获的大小不匹配时，引擎可以使用急切执行或将批次填充到捕获的大小。

捕获更多尺寸可以提高图形覆盖范围，但也会消耗更多 GPU 内存并增加启动时间。

因此 CUDA Graph 并不是通用的推理速度开关。

他们以灵活性和设置成本为代价换取较低的稳态启动开销。

下图显示了核心机制。

- 如果没有图表，CPU 会独立提交每个内核，并且可能会在 GPU 时间线上留下空闲间隙。
- 通过图表，序列被捕获一次并作为一个单元重播。

CUDA 图是为什么 LLM 推理需要专门的服务引擎而不是标准预测 API 的一个例子。

我们之前解释了传统 ML 推理和 LLM 推理之间的五个架构差异。

我们之前解释了传统 ML 推理和 LLM 推理之间的五个架构差异。

请阅读下面的内容。
titans.quote_en:
A tricky LLM interview question:

You move your LLM to a faster GPU.

Profiling confirms its kernels now finish sooner, but the time between generated tokens barely changes.

The model, precision, and batch size are identical.

Where did the expected speedup go?

(answer below)

An LLM forward pass is not one giant GPU operation.

It launches a sequence of operations for attention, matmul, normalization, sampling, data movement, and other work.

Without CUDA Graphs, the CPU prepares and submits these operations individually.

Each launch adds only a small amount of overhead, but token-by-token decoding repeats a similar sequence for every generated token.

This creates a strange bottleneck.

Some kernels finish in only a few microseconds. The GPU can complete one kernel before the CPU has submitted the next one.

That leaves empty spaces in a profiler trace. These gaps are not model computation. They show the GPU waiting for its next operation.

CUDA Graphs change how this work reaches the GPU.

The runtime captures a repeatable sequence of operations once, including their dependencies. Later iterations replay the captured sequence through one graph launch instead of submitting every operation separately.

To be clear, the kernels themselves do not become substantially faster.

Also, the model does not get smaller, and the forward pass performs almost the same computation.

Most of the gain comes from removing CPU launch work between kernels.

This is especially useful during LLM decoding.

Each decoding step processes one new token per sequence. This produces many short, repeated GPU operations where launch overhead can become a meaningful part of total latency.

Prefill often behaves differently.

A large prompt gives the GPU more parallel work, producing longer-running kernels. When those kernels already keep the GPU busy, reducing launch overhead matters less.

There is also a tradeoff.

A captured graph expects the same kernel sequence, stable arguments, fixed memory addresses, and a compatible execution structure on every replay.

Inference servers handle varying batch sizes and different prefill, mixed, and decode workloads. One captured graph cannot cover every execution path efficiently.

Engines such as vLLM and TensorRT-LLM therefore capture graphs for several common execution cases and batch sizes.

When a live batch does not match a captured size, the engine may use eager execution or pad the batch to a captured size.

Capturing more sizes improves graph coverage, but it also consumes more GPU memory and increases startup time.

So CUDA Graphs are not a universal inference speed switch.

They trade flexibility and setup cost for lower steady-state launch overhead.

The visual below shows the core mechanism.

- Without a graph, the CPU submits each kernel independently and may leave idle gaps on the GPU timeline.
- With a graph, the sequence is captured once and replayed as a unit.

CUDA Graphs are one example of why LLM inference needs a specialized serving engine rather than a standard prediction API.

We previously explained five architectural differences between traditional ML inference and LLM inference.
